verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The GSO harness recorded binary_reward 0 because the continuous gm_speedup_patch_commit score of 1.156 did not exceed the 1.700 pass threshold [1][4][5]. The task asked the agent to optimize the np.char.isalpha benchmark while preserving functional equivalence and pursuing the best possible speedup [3]. The agent added a specialized C fast path for contiguous Unicode isalpha in multiarraymodule.c and rebuilt NumPy [6], and the held-out verifier confirmed all three benchmark workloads passed equivalence checks after applying the patch [7]. However, the verifier grades speed against the known reference commit ef5e545 ('Add ufunc for np.char.isalpha'), not merely the unoptimized base checkout [5][8], and on those timings the patch mean was only about 1.16× faster than the reference commit (geometric mean across the three tests), well short of the required 1.70× [4][9]. The agent's own validation compared optimized code only to the slow baseline (~16.6×) on the prompt workload, ran pytest on defchararray, and declared success without measuring against the ufunc-level solution the benchmark targets [10][11]. The optimization was real and correct but materially weaker than the reference approach, so the task was not truly solved and the verifier rightly failed the rollout (TN).
